source.title: Exploring the genetic etiology across the continuum of the general psychopathology factor: a Swedish population-based family and twin study

confidence_rationale: Large family (580,891 sibling pairs) and twin (17,170 pairs) study showing that comorbidity across 10 psychiatric diagnoses is captured by a latent general psychopathology (p) factor with a stable, heritable (~0.41-0.45) genetic basis across its whole continuum. Strongly supports Q-064's comorbidity=axis-overlap and pleiotropy=shared-genetic-mechanism premises (a single set of common variants loads the shared factor). But the dominance of a single general factor is double-edged for Q-064: it is the clearest evidence that the latent axes are NOT independent, directly stressing the non-degeneracy precondition -- hence mixed.
failure_signatures: Comorbidity is so pervasively captured by ONE general factor that the separable-axis premise is threatened: if most shared variance loads a single p dimension, a multi-axis vulnerability vector risks collapsing toward one dominant axis (the degenerate-axes / vacuous-vector branch of Q-064).

Heritability of the p factor is moderate (~0.41-0.45) and shared across the continuum, so genetic predisposition does NOT fully determine expressed syndrome -- which supports the predisposition!=expression separation, but also means the vector's predisposition layer is intrinsically noisy/partial.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Psychiatric comorbidity across 10 register-based diagnoses is accounted for by a latent general psychopathology (p) factor; family analysis (580,891 sibling pairs) shows the association between siblings' p factors is linear across the whole range including the extreme, and twin group-heritability (0.42-0.45) matches individual-differences heritability (0.41), indicating the entire continuum of the p factor shares a common, largely common-variant genetic origin.
mapping.ree_translation: Q-064 proposes representing comorbidity as overlap in a latent vulnerability vector and pleiotropy as one mechanism loading multiple axes. This study is direct human evidence for both: comorbidity loads a shared latent factor (axis-overlap), and that factor has a common-variant genetic basis (one genetic mechanism loading many disorders = pleiotropy). It also speaks to the predisposition layer: the heritable p factor is the genetic-vulnerability quantity, distinct from which specific diagnosis is expressed.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The p factor is a SINGLE general dimension extracted from human diagnostic registers, not REE's multi-axis ARC-086 vulnerability space; its strength as a single factor is evidence that shared variance is concentrated, which works AGAINST Q-064's requirement that multiple axes be separable. The study supports the comorbidity/pleiotropy mechanics of the vector while raising the dimensionality/degeneracy concern; it does not measure REE's mechanisms.
mapping.source_context: Swedish population-based family + twin epidemiology using national psychiatric registers; quantitative-genetic decomposition of a latent factor.

confidence_components.notes: Very large, well-designed quantitative-genetic study (source_quality high). Mapping_fidelity moderate: it directly evidences comorbidity-as-shared-factor and pleiotropy-as-common-variants, but via a single general factor rather than a multi-axis space, so it speaks to two of Q-064's premises while stressing a third. Transfer risk moderate: human register diagnoses -> REE vulnerability axes is a substantial leap.
